title: Precision-profile evaluation and calibration pipeline for FP8/INT8 — batch & long-context perf
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build and validate a repeatable calibration and evaluation flow for FP8 and INT8 precision profiles, then measure throughput and latency across batching regimes and long-context workloads. This ticket covers: (1) a calibration runner that produces per-layer/per-channel scale factors using hybrid histogram+KL heuristics, (2) an accuracy validation harness comparing FP8/INT8 variants to FP16 baselines on representative eval sets, and (3) a perf matrix measuring p50/p95 latency and sustained throughput across batch sizes and sequence lengths (including 8k/32k/64k contexts) with and without KV cache reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration runner (calib-runner-v2) produces stable profiles for FP8 and INT8 on target models with seedable runs
End-to-end accuracy delta for candidate profiles is computed against FP16 baseline and summarized (per-task and aggregated), with clear pass/fail thresholds
Perf matrix generated (CSV + Grafana dashboard) showing throughput & latency across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16] and contexts [1k,8k,32k,64k] for both batching-on and batching-off modes
Bench includes KV cache on/off runs to demonstrate cache reuse effects on throughput/latency for long contexts
Artifacts (profiles, calib logs, eval results, perf CSVs, PRs) are uploaded to Confluence/Drive and linked from this ticket
test_plan: Run calib-runner-v2 on model rdx-7b and rdx-70b with 3 seeds per config; seed values: 42, 123, 999
Produce FP8 (E4M3) and INT8 symmetric profiles; capture per-layer scale histograms and overflow counts
Run e2e-eval-harness on validation sets: lm-eval/gpt-standard, customer-like instruction set (5000 utterances), and regression prompt set (200 prompts)
Perf harness: run streamer (latency-first) and batcher (throughput-first) with target token rate ramps up to 200k tokens/s where hardware permits
Collect p50/p90/p95 latency and sustained throughput; repeat with KV cache warm and cold states
results_summary: Calibration: hybrid hist+KL produced lower per-layer scale variance vs naive min/max clipping; FP8 profiles had fewer overflow events than earlier FP8 configs (reduction ~3.2x on rdx-7b sample run)
Accuracy: FP8 (E4M3) candidate profiles show median absolute LM loss delta of +0.8% vs FP16 on lm-eval; INT8 symmetric shows +1.9% but with tighter tail variance on instruction-following tasks

Perf: For rdx-7b at batch=8, seq=8k with KV-cache warm, FP8 maintained 92% of FP16 throughput while reducing GPU memory footprint by ~30%. INT8 hit 110% effective tokens/s in throughput-limited configs but increased p95 latency by 12% under tail-heavy request mixes

Long-context: at 64k context, batching interaction dominated latency — continuous batching collapsed p95 by ~25% compared to single-request handling, but memory pressure required quant profile adjustments to avoid OOMs on 80GB GPUs
Failure modes: INT8 symmetric occasionally produced token-level hallucination spikes on a small subset of prompt families; flagged for targeted per-layer recalibration and fallback policies
dev_notes: Implemented hybrid histogram approach in calib-runner-v2: per-channel channel-aware binning + KL-based cutoff. Initial runs used 2048-bin histograms then switched to adaptive bins for memory reduction.
Added overflow counters and a lightweight sanity-check pass that rejects profiles with >0.5% overflow rate on sample inputs
Changed kernel selection to prefer int8 GEMM for layers where activation range stability is high; fallback path kept for layers flagged by calibrator

Observed batching microqueue contention when using our default batching window (12ms). Reduced batching window to 6ms for low-latency experiments which improved p95 but reduced aggregated throughput under heavy load
KV cache reuse: reused cached KV stores across requests where conversation_id matched; noticed throughput gains of 18–26% for multi-turn workloads
next_steps: Run extended stability sweep across 10 customer workloads to validate INT8 hallucination spikes and identify problematic prompt patterns
Automate profile selection into runtime: tag profiles with "quality labels" (pass/soft-fail/block) and add canary rollout to Dedicated pools
Add quant-aware memory estimator to console so Dedicated customers can preview memory footprint changes with FP8/INT8
Prepare runtime-1.19 release note summarizing safe profiles and recommended fallback policies
